html:
The map's name, in its 1900 snapshot, for the original realm of Samori Ture on the upper Niger, in what are now eastern Guinea and south-western Mali, with its capital at Bissandugu. It is the first phase of his Wassoulou Empire.

Samori built it in the 1870s and 1880s from Malinke and Wassoulou chiefdoms, ruling as a Muslim almamy. After years of fighting and treaties, the French invaded it in force from 1891. Samori fell back east, burning the land behind him, and founded his Second Empire. By 1900 this land was part of French West Africa.
